subject: math

entries: The two seed identities, on the unit circle - the legs are cos theta and sin theta with hypotenuse 1, so sin squared plus cos squared equals one and tan is sin over cos.
slots.label: The two seed identities, on the unit circle
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Compound angles: computing sin 75 degrees - split 75 as 45 + 30, expand with sin(A + B), and the four known values give (root 6 + root 2) over 4.
slots.label: Compound angles: computing sin 75 degrees
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The R-formula: one wobble, not two - 3 cos x + 4 sin x becomes 5 cos(x - 53.1 degrees) from the 3-4-5 triangle, so max is 5 and min is -5.
slots.label: The R-formula: one wobble, not two
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Misconception: cos(A + B) does not split - cos 60 is 0.5 while cos 30 + cos 30 is about 1.73, so the cosine of a sum is never the sum of cosines.
slots.label: Misconception: cos(A + B) does not split
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: An equation true for every value of the angle, such as sin squared theta + cos squared theta = 1, which comes from the unit circle with hypotenuse 1.
slots.label: Identity
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An angle formed by adding or subtracting two angles, such as 75 degrees as 45 + 30, handled with formulae like sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B.
slots.label: Compound angle
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The rewrite a cos x + b sin x = R cos(x - alpha), where R is the square root of a squared plus b squared and tan alpha = b over a, giving one wave of amplitude R.
slots.label: R-formula
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The circle of radius 1 centred at the origin; a point at angle theta has coordinates (cos theta, sin theta), which is why the seed identity holds.
slots.label: Unit circle
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: A-Math trigonometry: identities, compound angles and the R-formula
